children.name: Brooklands
children.content:
Soaring heights are achieved at Brooklands – a two-Michelin starred rooftop restaurant that is both a destination and a journey. The space, which pays homage to the classic eras of British aviation and motorsport, sets the scene for the modern British cuisine of Chef Director Claude Bosi. 

Brooklands shares its namesake with the storied Surrey racetrack – the birthplace of British racing sport and flight innovation. The restaurant, as well as its dedicated lift and entryway, are appointed with a specially curated collection of artefacts honouring Brooklands’ history. Amongst the most remarkable of these is a vintage Napier Railton, the 1933 race car that set – and still holds – Brooklands’ speed record; and an arresting scale-model of the iconic Concorde aircraft, suspended from the ceiling of the main dining room. These are also reflected in the restaurant’s two private dining rooms – ‘Napier Railton’ and ‘Mach II’. A wall of floor-to-ceiling windows, and a terrace with stunning views of London’s skyline only further enhance the sense of being airborne. 

Brooklands offers a menu crafted from the very best of British ingredients using traditional French techniques to deliver dishes that perfectly balance modernity and classic fine dining. Together, Chef Director Claude Bosi and Chef de Cuisine Francesco Dibenedetto bring a wealth of culinary expertise to establish Brooklands as a highly desirable and respected drinking and dining destination. 

For enquiries or to make a reservation, please contact the Hotel Operator. 

Lunch:
12:00pm – 13:30pm (Thursday to Saturday) 
Dinner: 
6:00pm – 9:45pm, Tuesday to Saturday (Last seating at 9:30pm and Last Order at 9:45pm) 
*Closed on Sundays and Mondays

children.name: Brooklands Bar
children.content:
A sleek space showcasing innovative cocktails, as well as striking views across London’s skyline, Brooklands Bar makes an unforgettable day-to-night rooftop destination. An array of classic cocktails can be savoured here, along with more conceptual cocktails specially developed in our ‘Drinks Studio’. 

The bar’s design further embraces the restaurant’s themes of classic British aviation, motorsport, and fine craftsmanship. Its intricate latticed ceiling echoes that of a twin-engine bomber designed in the 1930s; its striking glass chandelier, meanwhile, replicates the blades of a Rolls Royce turbine jet engine.

For enquiries or to make a reservation, please contact the Hotel Operator.

children.name: The Tasting Room
children.content:
Occupying an exclusive area of the rooftop, The Tasting Room cigar lounge offers an elegant and relaxed space for the enjoyment of finely curated cigars. The walk-in humidor, along with a collection of rare top-shelf whiskies, is overseen by Master of Havana Cigars Manu Harit. Patrons can also rent private climate-controlled lockers for storing their cigar purchases. 

Like the adjacent Brooklands restaurant and bar – with which it shares a dedicated elevator – The Tasting Room takes design inspiration from the world of fine motorcars. Its mahogany-panelled sitting room incorporates design elements of The Delage 155B, a luxury French race car that won the first Grand Prix at Brooklands in 1926. The lounge and attached terrace also afford truly breath-taking panoramic views over Hyde Park and the surrounding cityscape.

children.name: Canton Blue
children.content:
Celebrating the convergence of Asian and British cultures through historic maritime trade routes, Canton Blue offers innovative Cantonese cuisine in a collection of exquisitely decorated spaces.

The restaurant’s main dining room invokes the shared heritage of transcontinental sea trade between China and Britain, known as The Maritime Silk Road. Numerous design elements take inspiration from the Keying junk, a trade ship that connected the two countries during the mid-19th century – including displays of Cantonese porcelain, which the ship carried from East to West; and a magnificent backlit ceiling panel depicting a celestial navigation map. The low-lit tables and intimate private booths centre around a carved, dual-aspect fireplace, shared with an adjacent tea lounge. Two private dining rooms – The Silk Room and The Music Room – each celebrate a distinctive facet of Chinese culture. Throughout Canton Blue, the service, like the décor and cuisine, is refined and striking, with many dishes finished tableside.

For enquiries or to make a reservation, please contact the Hotel Operator.

children.name: Little Blue
children.content:
Continuing the exotic sensory journey of Canton Blue, Little Blue offers sophisticated cocktails, fine spirits, and artisanal teas in a glamourous, intimate setting. The bar’s décor reflects a harmonious blend of British and Chinese history, with classic leather seats, etched glass, and a wall of apothecary-style spice cabinets that nod to the spice trade routes of the Keying junk. The drink offerings also embrace the confluence of the two cultures: many cocktails incorporate Asian fruits, spices, and herbal tinctures as well as premier spirits; and an extensive menu of teas that can be taken in both the English and Chinese traditions. 

For enquiries or to make a reservation, please contact the Hotel Operator.

children.name: Bletchley Park
children.content:
Private Tour and Dinner
One of Britain’s most famous great houses, Bletchley Park is the legendary site where World War II code-breakers changed the course of history. Guests taking part in this program will be driven to Bletchley Park via The Peninsula London’s luxury fleet, and met there by Sir Dermot Turing – the nephew of renowned mathematician, computer scientist, and cryptanalyst Alan Turing, who helped to crack the Enigma code. Sir Dermot will lead guests on a private tour of the historic grounds of Bletchley Park, uncovering secrets of the house and delving into the pivotal moments that shortened the war and revolutionized modern computing. Guests will also enjoy a three-course dinner with Sir Dermot in Bletchley Park’s Ballroom before returning to The Peninsula.

children.name: Concorde Legacy
children.content:
Concorde Legacy Experience at Brooklands
Among the many historic feats of British aviation pioneered at Brooklands, none is as iconic as the conception and manufacture of the ground-breaking Concorde. This full-day programme lets guests experience the superb innovation and opulence of this supersonic aircraft. The adventure begins with a drive to Brooklands Museum via Rolls-Royce sedan; after welcome tea in a plush Edwardian departure lounge, they will board the museum’s own BAC Aerospatiale Concorde (known as the Delta Golf), for a Champagne-accompanied tour of its interior and flight deck. Following a three-course lunch with former chief Concorde pilots Mike Bannister and John Ty, each guest will spend 45 thrilling minutes at the controls of the Concorde Simulator. After returning to The Peninsula London, they can share their impressions of the day over a seven-course tasting menu at Brooklands restaurant.

This exclusive experience brings guests on a curated tour of the magnificent Crown Jewels, a dazzling collection of gems that has been guarded in the Tower of London since 1661. After seeing and learning about these treasures, including the Imperial State Crown and Queen Mary's Crown – originally made by Garrard, the Royal family’s first Crown Jeweller, in 1911, and subsequently modified for the 2023 coronation of Her Majesty Queen Camilla – guests will get a private gemmology masterclass led by Garrard's in-house gemmologist. Held at The Peninsula London’s Garrard boutique, the class will include service of signature Peninsula Afternoon Tea, and the chance to try on replica Royal tiaras worn by famous queens and princesses.

This exceptional opportunity allows guests to sit for a private portrait with renowned Royal artist Ralph Heimans – whose captivating works have included portraits of Queen Elizabeth II, The Duke of Edinburgh, and The Prince of Wales (now His Royal Majesty King Charles). This exciting family-friendly quest lets children and their parents be secret agents for a day. Their mission: To track down and recover a prized spice mix, which has been pilfered from The Peninsula London’s acclaimed chef, in time to host an important banquet. This iconic museum is home to a truly staggering collection of artworks, which span almost every conceivable medium and span more than 5,000 years. It permanently houses nearly 3 million works of painting, sculpture, photography, architecture, ceramics, textiles, glass, and jewellery; its majestic galleries also host visiting exhibits, talks, and hands-on workshops. children.name: Hyde Park
children.content:
London W2 2UH

The largest of the Royal Parks and one of London’s most beloved central green spaces, Hyde Park encompasses 350 acres of rolling lawns, gardens, play spaces and sporting courts. All are connected by paths popular with walkers and cyclists and punctuated with picnic spots. Through the middle of the park winds the 40-acre Serpentine Lake, a favourite spot for renting rowboats, lounging on the lido, and waterside dining.

One of the park’s highlights is its spectacular Rose Garden, with beds and trellises that burst into bloom every summer. Another is its many significant memorials and works of statuary, including the Princess Diana Memorial Fountain. And a true don’t-miss Hyde Park experience is visiting Speaker’s Corner, a location since 1872 for free-speech debates and demonstrations – which still take place today.

children.name: Green Park
children.content:
London SW1A 1BW

Less than five minutes’ walk from The Peninsula London, the peaceful beauty of Green Park beckons. A 40-acre, triangle-shaped oasis set between Constitution Hill and Piccadilly, the park is quiet and verdant, with grassy lawns shaded by mature native oak, hawthorn, and silver maple trees. There are no formal gardens here, but each spring 250,000 daffodils burst into bloom carpeting the park in brilliant yellow.

The park’s entrance is marked by the grand Canada Gate, given to England by Canada as a memorial to Queen Victoria. Three other Green Park memorials – the Canada Memorial, the Memorial Gates, and the Bomber Command Memorial – pay tribute to the thousands who lost their lives in service to England during the World Wars. During special state visits and royal birthdays, the park hosts The King's Troop, Royal Horse Artillery, which performs a Royal Gun Salute.

children.name: St. James's Park
children.content:
Bordered by Buckingham Palace, The Mall, and Horse Guards Parade, the impeccably manicured, 58-acre St James’s is perhaps the most formal of the Royal Parks. It is where many ceremonial events take place, including the annual Trooping the Colour on the King’s birthday. It is also home to some of the most famously spectacular gardens in London: The Memorial Gardens fronting Buckingham Palace. Originally planted in 1901 as a memorial to Queen Victoria, the semi-circular gardens contain 22,500 plants, including scarlet geraniums that match the tunics of The Queen's Guard.

The park centres around the long St. James’s Park Lake, where numerous birds and waterfowl live, feed, and nest – most remarkably, pelicans. The birds have actually lived in St. James’s Park for nearly 400 years, since the first pelicans were presented as a gift from the Russian Ambassador to King Charles II.

children.name: Skincare
children.content:
The Peninsula Spa & Wellness Centre partners with leading wellness brands to offer a holistic collection of the world’s finest spa and beauty experiences. Partners include high-performance beauty brand Margy’s and Ayurveda aromatherapy specialist Subtle Energies, as well as a carefully considered roster of resident practitioners and opportunities for outdoor activity in the adjacent Royal Parks. 

Subtle Energies
The Australia-based results-driven aromatherapy and natural skincare line provides wellness solutions founded on authentic Ayurveda principles. Subtle Energies treatments are created with intent to address multiple skin and body concerns, whilst delivering high performance results empowering one’s physical, mental and emotional wellbeing. All products are made in Australia, following European standards of natural skincare, to create safe, ethical and effective products. The range has been certified by Cruelty-Free International and does not contain parabens, mineral oils, silicones or artificial fragrances.

Margy’s 
Favoured by celebrities around the globe, Margy’s renowned beauty treatments and formulas can be experienced exclusively at The Peninsula Spa. Margy’s Monte Carlo is an instant, results-driven, anti-ageing programme featuring highly effective facial treatments that incorporate rare, active ingredients and high-quality, Swiss-made products developed specifically to target the signs of ageing. Founder Margie Lombard’s vision is to provide the skin with the natural ingredients while focusing on deep, precise manual techniques combined with her product formulations, which take inspiration from nature to care for the skin.
